title: PDF / Anyar Myay Coalition Captures Junta Militia Base in Myaing, Magway — 49 Civilians Rescued from Pyu Saw Htee Control
detail: People's Defence Force (PDF) fighters and the Anyar Myay Coalition Force on May 26, 2026 seized the Myanmar junta army and Pyu Saw Htee (pro-junta Pyusawti) militia camp at Thayetkan Village, Myaing Township, Magway Region, rescuing 49 civilians — including women and children — who had been held under militia control. Weapons and ammunition were confiscated in the operation. The capture gave resistance forces improved access to key transport routes in Myaing Township. Myaing Township is part of the contested Magway-Sagaing corridor where the junta has conducted intensive multi-front operations in May 2026, including the multi-township Pauk/Saw/Kyaukhtu offensive (May 13-14) and the sustained ground campaign in Kani Township (Sagaing Region). The Pyu Saw Htee are pro-junta civilian militia established by the SAC as a supplement to regular Tatmadaw forces, tasked with village-level surveillance, arrest operations, and counter-insurgency in areas where the military cannot maintain permanent garrisons. Resistance forces have prioritized dismantling Pyu Saw Htee networks across Sagaing and Magway regions because the militias collect intelligence, conduct extrajudicial killings, and facilitate collective punishment of civilian communities in PDF-controlled areas. The rescue of 49 civilians adds to a pattern of resistance forces liberating communities from militia-enforced detention — a practice the junta uses to deprive PDF fighters of civilian support networks. On the following day (May 27), two mine detonations on junta forces retreating from the Thayetkan area killed 2 SAC soldiers and wounded 6 others, reflecting continued resistance follow-on operations in Myaing Township.

media.caption: PDF and Anyar Myay Coalition forces capture Pyu Saw Htee militia camp in Thayetkan Village, Myaing Township, Magway Region — 49 civilians rescued; Myanmar Now, May 26, 2026

title: KIA-Aligned Resistance FPV Drone Kills 5 Junta Soldiers in Bhamo Township, Kachin State
detail: Kachin Independence Army-aligned resistance forces on May 26, 2026 conducted a first-person view (FPV) drone attack on junta army formations in Bhamo Township, Kachin State, killing five Myanmar military soldiers. The strike reflects the continued application of precision drone warfare in the KIA's multi-front Kachin campaign even as the KIA shifted to a declared defensive strategy on May 22 following the SAC's deployment of a 300-vehicle armored convoy with mobile howitzers to the Northern Military Command headquarters in Myitkyina. Bhamo is an active KIA-junta frontline on the Irrawaddy River corridor in southern Kachin State; KIA-led forces have seized multiple junta military camps in Bhamo and Waingmaw districts throughout May 2026, including the tightening of KIA encirclement of Infantry Battalion 58 in Waingmaw to within 100 meters of the base. The May 26 FPV drone strike demonstrates that the KIA's announced tactical defensive posture has not halted localized offensive operations — particularly precision drone strikes — in Bhamo District. FPV drones have become a primary infantry-level weapon for Myanmar's resistance forces, allowing fighters to conduct kinetic strikes on junta formations without exposing themselves to ground fire or requiring artillery support. The strike comes two days before May 28, when Bhamo marks 100 days since the onset of the current phase of intensified KIA operations in the district.

media.caption: KIA-aligned FPV drone kills 5 junta soldiers in Bhamo Township, Kachin State — despite KIA's announced May 22 defensive strategy shift, precision drone operations continue along Irrawaddy River corridor; Mizzima Spring Revolution Daily, May 26, 2026
